## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`Cache.set` must lower-case its key before merge: it stores under the raw key while `get` looks up only the lower-cased key, so any entry written with an upper-case letter is unreadable. The added tests were read, not run.

## Changes
The pull request adds `Cache.set` to `app/cache.py` and raises `DEFAULT_TTL` from 60 to 300 seconds, updating the comment to match. It adds three tests in `tests/test_cache.py`: a set/get round trip, the constant's value, and expiry.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Lower-case the key in Cache.set — `set("Alpha", 1)` followed by `get("Alpha")` returns `None`: line 27 writes `self._store[key]` while `get` reads and deletes only `key.lower()` (lines 17 and 22). The comment at lines 14–15, "every path into _store lower-cases the key first", becomes false. — Any value stored under a key containing an upper-case letter is unreadable and never evicted, so `_store` grows without bound. — Fix: Write to `self._store[key.lower()]` and extend `test_set_then_get_round_trip` in `tests/test_cache.py`, which only sets the lower-case key `"alpha"`, with a mixed-case `set` key.

## Suggestions
- tests/test_cache.py:18 — tests — Assert default expiry behavior, not the constant — Changing the constructor default at `app/cache.py:10` to a literal such as `ttl=60` leaves `test_default_ttl_is_five_minutes` passing, because it compares `Cache.DEFAULT_TTL` to 300 without building a cache. The only expiry test, `test_entries_expire`, passes `ttl=1`. — No test protects the 300-second expiry of a `Cache()` built without arguments, which is the behavior this pull request changes. — Fix: Extend `test_entries_expire` with a `Cache()` case that advances the patched clock to just before and just after 300 seconds.
